Asclepiades was gripped by great grief,
because the earth and its inhabitants had been deprived of his blessings and his ministry.
And he depicted his image very wonderfully, as one who was being taken up to heaven,
and he set up the statue of Hermes in the temple in which he used to pray and worship God.
And whenever he went in there,
he would sit before it just as during his lifetime,
and he would receive a blessing from him.
And it is said
that this deed became the origin of the worship of idols in the world.
The Greeks, however, many generations later, supposed concerning that statue,
that it was the statue of Asclepiades.
And for this reason they magnified him greatly,
and they used to swear by him before Christianity.
For Hippocrates said:
"I adjure you,
my disciples,
by the Creator of death and of life, and by my father and your father, Asclepiades."
And he further said that his name, it is said, is derived by etymology from beauty, light, and medicine.
Therefore, it is fitting for every physician to resemble him in purity, chastity, and holiness.
And Galen said
that one should not deny the healing that happens to the sick whenever they enter the temple of Asclepiades.
And Hippocrates said
that his staff, on which he leaned, was of almond wood {OCR?}.
And Galen said
that in this way he hinted at the moderation that is virtuous,
in that almond wood {OCR?} is tempered between hot and cold.
After Enoch, Methuselah his son, being one hundred and sixty-seven years old, begat Lamech.
All his days were nine hundred and sixty-two years.
At the age of one hundred and eighty-eight years, he begat Noah.
All his days were seven hundred and seventy-three (773) years.
This one died before his father.
After Lamech, Noah his son.
At the age of five hundred years, he begat Shem.
All his days were nine hundred and fifty years.
And in his six-hundredth year,
the Flood occurred on the twenty-seventh of Iyyar,
when there was violent rain for forty days;
and the waters increased and lifted up the ark which Noah had made,
and into it had entered he, his wife, his three sons, and their wives, by the command of God.
And the waters rose fifteen cubits above the high mountains.
Then the wrath was appeased.
